issues.legal_issue: A highest bidder whose bid has not been accepted and who has not received an allotment letter has no vested right to the property and cannot obtain an order compelling allotment through a suit for declaration and mandatory injunction.
material_facts: The plaintiff submitted the highest bid and paid the required initial deposit at the auction.
The competent authority did not accept the bid, and no allotment letter was issued.
The plaintiff sought a declaration that rejection was illegal and a mandatory order requiring allotment.
The court could not itself accept the bid; a declaration that the rejection was unlawful would not establish a concluded contract.
issues.conclusion: The suit, in the form filed, was not maintainable for the relief sought, and mandatory allotment could not be ordered in the absence of an accepted bid and an allotment letter.
issues.legal_principle: Under Regulation 6(2) of the Haryana Urban Development (Disposal of Land and Buildings) Regulations, 1978, acceptance by the competent authority and issuance of the allotment letter precede the further payment obligation and formation of a concluded contract. A highest bidder acquires no vested right merely by making the highest bid or paying a deposit. The Court relied on Uttar Pradesh Avas Evam Vikas Parishad v. Om Prakash Sharma (2013) 5 SCC 182, including its discussion of Rajasthan Housing Board v. G.S. Investments (2007) 1 SCC 477 and State of Orissa v. Harinarayan Jaiswal (1972) 2 SCC 36.

rule.if: civil_suit_seeking_allotment and bid_not_accepted and allotment_letter_not_issued and (highest_bid_submitted or initial_deposit_paid)

predicates.civil_suit_seeking_allotment: The bidder brought a civil suit seeking a declaration about rejection of the bid and an order requiring allotment.
predicates.bid_not_accepted: The competent authority did not accept the bidder’s offer.
predicates.allotment_letter_not_issued: The authority did not issue an allotment letter to the bidder.
predicates.highest_bid_submitted: The bidder submitted the highest offer at the auction.
predicates.initial_deposit_paid: The bidder paid the initial deposit required at the auction.

issues.definition: When a bidder seeks allotment in a civil suit but the offer remains unaccepted and no allotment letter has issued, submitting the highest offer or paying an initial deposit does not enable the bidder to compel allotment.

issues.legal_issue: An auction presiding officer who is authorized by the auction terms and the authority’s delegation may reject a bid, subject to the scope of that authorization.
material_facts: The auction terms reserved to the presiding officer the right to reject any bid.
The Administrator presided over the auction and later rejected the bids.
The authority had delegated auction-bid functions to the Administrator, and the bidder had not challenged the delegation order.
The delegation provided for the Administrator to accept specified bids when the stated conditions were met; the auction terms independently reserved a right to reject bids.
issues.conclusion: The Administrator had authority to reject the bids as presiding officer under the auction terms and under the delegation that had not been challenged.
issues.legal_principle: Section 51(1) of the Haryana Urban Development Authority Act, 1977, permitted delegation by the Authority. The Court relied on the delegation order and the auction term reserving the presiding officer’s power to reject a bid. It held that, absent a challenge to the delegation, the bidder could not invalidate it by asserting that delegation under section 51(4) was required.

rule.if: public_authority_property_auction and official_was_auction_presiding_officer and auction_terms_reserved_bid_rejection_power and delegation_was_not_challenged

predicates.public_authority_property_auction: A public authority conducted an auction for its property.
predicates.official_was_auction_presiding_officer: The official who rejected the bid had presided over the auction.
predicates.auction_terms_reserved_bid_rejection_pow: The announced auction terms reserved to the presiding officer the power to reject a bid.
predicates.delegation_was_not_challenged: The bidder did not challenge the authority’s delegation of auction functions to the official.

issues.definition: In a public authority’s property auction, an official who presided over it and had a rejection power reserved by the auction terms was authorized to reject a bid where the delegation of functions was not challenged.

issues.legal_issue: Rejection of the highest bid is not arbitrary where the authorized decision-maker considers relevant reports and market information and gives a reasoned public-interest basis for rejecting the bids.
material_facts: The Administrator rejected seven bids rather than only the plaintiff’s bid.
The rejection communication recorded that relevant reports and aspects had been examined.
The auction committee’s recommendations and comparative price information indicated that the prices fetched were considered low in relation to market trends for similar property elsewhere.
The authority stated that the decision was taken to protect public revenue, and the Court found that the decision reflected application of mind.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the bids was justified and was not illegal or arbitrary; the rejection was not open to interference on the grounds advanced.
issues.legal_principle: A public authority is not obliged to accept the highest bid and may reject it for good and sufficient reasons, but its decision must be free from arbitrariness or favouritism and reasons should be available. The Court relied on State of U.P. v. Vijay Bahadur Singh (1982) 2 SCC 365, Laxmikant v. Satyawan (1996) 4 SCC 208, Meerut Development Authority v. Association of Management Studies (2009) 6 SCC 171, and M/s. Star Enterprises v. City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Ltd. (1990) 3 SCC 280. It also applied Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner (1978) 1 SCC 405, explaining that the reasons here were reflected in the rejection decision and the reports considered; a bid above the reserve price alone did not require acceptance.

rule.if: public_auction_bid_rejection_review and decision_maker_had_rejection_authority and rejection_decision_recorded_consideration_of_reports and market_information_supported_low_price_assessment and multiple_bids_were_rejected

predicates.public_auction_bid_rejection_review: A court reviewed a public authority’s decision to reject a bid made at auction.
predicates.decision_maker_had_rejection_authority: The official who made the rejection decision was authorized to reject bids.
predicates.rejection_decision_recorded_consideratio: The rejection decision recorded that relevant reports and aspects had been considered.
predicates.market_information_supported_low_price_a: Comparative market information supported the authority’s assessment that the prices offered were low.
predicates.multiple_bids_were_rejected: The authority rejected several bids in the same auction rather than rejecting only the bidder’s offer.

issues.definition: A rejection of an auction bid is not arbitrary when an authorized decision-maker records consideration of reports, relies on market information supporting a low-price assessment, and rejects multiple bids.

issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking mandatory allotment of property must bear ad valorem court fee assessed by reference to the value of the transaction rather than nominal valuation.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought mandatory allotment of the property after submitting a bid.
The plaintiff valued the suit nominally and paid a nominal court fee.
The requested relief would require the court to direct allotment of property for which the bid stated a transaction value.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was required to pay ad valorem court fee, with the suit valuation reflecting the bid amount, before the trial court and the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a plaintiff seeking mandatory injunction for issuance of an allotment letter must pay ad valorem court fee based on the value of the transaction. No specific statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion in the judgment.

predicates.civil_suit_seeking_mandatory_allotment: The plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking an order requiring allotment of property.
predicates.nominal_court_fee_paid: The plaintiff valued the suit nominally and paid only a nominal court fee.
predicates.property_transaction_value_identified: The bid or other case material identified a transaction value for the property.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks mandatory allotment in a civil suit, has paid only nominal court fee, and the property transaction value is identified, ad valorem court fee is required.
